domain_label: Plated-Jewelry Market — Trend-Signal Reading & Public-Storefront Competitor / Price-Tier Mapping
purpose: A method for reading US fashion/costume-jewelry demand from public trend signals (search-query volume, social/marketplace signals, retail assortment newness) with each signal's lag and bias made explicit, building a competitor and price-tier landscape map from publicly observable storefront attributes, and separating durable demand from fad, so the owner's launch decision is fed ranked category/tier priorities without ever inventing a market size, a competitor's sales, or naming any brand as a verified owner-competitor.
assumptions: no proprietary sales, market-share, or competitor-revenue data is available; every signal used is publicly observable (search-trend indices, public social engagement counts, public marketplace ranks/review counts, public retail storefront listings) [FACT-scope]
public trend signals are ordinal, relative, and lagged proxies for demand intent, not cardinal measures of units sold; a signal's direction is more trustworthy than its level [FACT-method]

US FTC Jewelry Guides 16 CFR Part 23 supply the finish definitions used to normalize competitor claims (gold-plated, gold-filled, vermeil = >=10k gold >=2.5um over sterling silver, rhodium as a platinum-group white metal, sterling = 92.5% Ag) [FACT-16 CFR 23]

the competitor set is defined as public storefront CATEGORIES (DTC plated-fashion, marketplace sellers, fast-fashion accessory, demi-fine adjacent), never as a specific named brand asserted to be the owner's verified competitor [METHOD-honesty]
listed storefront price is not realized price; discounts, promos, bundles and returns move realized price, so the price-tier ladder is built from listed prices with that gap flagged [FACT-method]

every non-fact is tagged [ESTIMATE] (method+confidence) or [UNKNOWN]; real regulatory/method facts are tagged [FACT] with basis; no market size, unit count, solid-vs-plated share, demographic rate, brand claim, or price is stated as measured
exclusions: the category/finish demand-structure taxonomy and the solid-vs-plated share method (that is kb1_category_and_finish_demand; this KB reads trend signals and maps competitors on top of it)
consumer demographic/ethnic/age segmentation method (that is kb2_consumer_segmentation_method; this KB reads aggregate trend and competitor signals, not who the buyer is)
the paid IG/TikTok poll instrument, incentive and sampling design (that is the S4 poll specialist; this KB reads pre-existing public social signals, not a commissioned poll)
the final 6-SKU launch pick and its production constraints (that is the S5 assortment specialist; this KB stops at ranked category/tier priorities and a positioning map)
asserting an actual market size, unit-sales figure, competitor revenue/margin, solid-vs-plated percentage, or any single named brand as a verified competitor with measured share

competency_questions.question: What public trend-signal sources exist for US fashion-jewelry demand, and how are they categorized and scoped to the owner's launch decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_AND_DECISION_FRAME states the decisions the map must serve (which categories/tiers to prioritize) and the no-invented-numbers/no-verified-brand honesty boundary, and SIGNAL_TAXONOMY enumerates the signal families (search-query volume, social engagement, marketplace rank/review, retail assortment newness, editorial trend forecast) as public and ordinal

competency_questions.question: How is a search-trend signal read as demand intent, and what lag and bias must be corrected for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEARCH_TREND_SIGNAL states that search indices are relative-not-absolute, sampled, seasonally and geographically skewed, and lead purchase by an intent-to-buy lag, and SIGNAL_LAG_BIAS_LEDGER places its lead/lag and biases in the cross-signal ledger

competency_questions.question: How is a social-platform signal (IG/TikTok hashtag/sound/engagement) read, and why does virality bias it toward fad?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOCIAL_PLATFORM_SIGNAL states that engagement is algorithmically amplified, creator/sponsored-contaminated, and skews toward novelty/virality that overstates durable demand, with the [METHOD] to read it and SIGNAL_LAG_BIAS_LEDGER carrying its bias

competency_questions.question: How can a public marketplace best-seller rank or review velocity be used as a sales proxy, and what are its limits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKETPLACE_SIGNAL states that best-seller rank is ordinal not cardinal, that review count is a lagged and under-counted sales proxy (review rate << purchase rate), and gives the [METHOD] to convert rank/review-velocity into a relative demand signal without inventing unit counts

competency_questions.question: How does retail assortment newness / restock cadence reveal supply-side preference, and why is it a lagging signal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETAIL_NEWNESS_SIGNAL states that new-arrival cadence and implied restock are a revealed-preference signal of what retailers bet on, lagging actual demand by the buy-plan cycle, with survivorship bias toward winners already on shelf

competency_questions.question: What is each signal's lead/lag relative to actual purchase, and what systematic biases does each carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIGNAL_LAG_BIAS_LEDGER tabulates, per signal family, its lead/lag versus purchase and its dominant bias (self-selection, survivorship, algorithmic amplification, seasonality, ordinal-not-cardinal), so no single signal is read at face value

competency_questions.question: How is the competitor set defined honestly from public storefronts without naming any brand as a verified owner-competitor?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITOR_FRAME_DEFINITION defines competitor CATEGORIES (DTC plated-fashion, marketplace seller, fast-fashion accessory, demi-fine adjacent) not verified named rivals, and STOREFRONT_SAMPLING_METHOD gives the [METHOD] to build and provenance a sample from public discovery paths with its sampling bias flagged

competency_questions.question: How is a competitor and price-tier map built from publicly observable storefront attributes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PUBLIC_ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA lists the observable per-SKU attributes (category, finish claim, materials claim, listed price, size range, positioning copy), and PRICE_TIER_LADDER builds price brackets from listed prices while flagging the listed-vs-realized-price gap

competency_questions.question: How are competitor finish claims normalized so they are comparable and puffery is flagged?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINISH_CLAIM_NORMALIZATION maps storefront finish wording onto the FTC 16 CFR Part 23 definitions (gold-plated / gold-filled / vermeil >=10k >=2.5um over sterling / rhodium / sterling 92.5%) and flags non-compliant or vague claims as [UNKNOWN]-quality, never treating marketing copy as a measured spec

competency_questions.question: How is a positioning map built and read for competitive whitespace in the owner's fashion/costume tier?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POSITIONING_MAP places sampled SKUs on price-tier x finish/style axes as a map (not a ranking), and WHITESPACE_DETECTION reads crowding and gaps as [ESTIMATE] whitespace hypotheses to be confirmed, not asserted openings

competency_questions.question: How is durable demand separated from fad, and how is a trend staged on its lifecycle to time entry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DURABLE_VS_FAD_DISCRIMINATORS states the [FACT-method] discriminators (trend duration, seasonally-adjusted baseline persistence, breadth across cohorts/platforms, replenishment vs novelty nature) and TREND_LIFECYCLE_STAGING places a trend on the emerging/growth/peak/decline curve and flags late-at-peak fad entry

competency_questions.question: Why must a read be triangulated across independent signals before acting, and how is that done?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIGNAL_TRIANGULATION requires agreement across >=2-3 independent signal families before a category/trend is treated as actionable and names the single-signal traps (a viral spike with no search or marketplace confirmation) it prevents

competency_questions.question: How are demand durability and whitespace scored for the launch, and what is handed off honestly to the assortment decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_DURABILITY_SCORE composes an [ESTIMATE] rank of candidate categories by durable-demand strength x whitespace, HONESTY_LEDGER separates the [FACT] method/regulatory anchors from the [ESTIMATE] reads and the [UNKNOWN] true sales/share/price-realization, and TREND_COMPETITOR_HANDOFF delivers ranked category/tier priorities plus the positioning map with every tag, stopping before the SKU pick

glossary.definition: A publicly observable proxy for demand intent or momentum - search-query volume, social hashtag/sound/engagement, marketplace best-seller rank / review velocity, retail assortment newness, or editorial trend forecast - each of which is ordinal, relative and lagged, and none of which is a measured count of units sold.

A per-signal table of how far each signal leads or lags actual purchase and what systematic bias it carries (self-selection, survivorship, algorithmic amplification, seasonality, ordinal-not-cardinal), used so no single signal is read at face value and disagreements are interpreted rather than averaged away.

An ordinal signal ranks options (marketplace best-seller rank says A outsells B, not by how much); a cardinal signal would state a magnitude (units sold). Public jewelry-demand signals are ordinal/relative; treating them as cardinal is the core fabrication risk this KB forbids.

The honest definition of the competitor set as public storefront CATEGORIES - DTC plated-fashion, marketplace seller, fast-fashion accessory, demi-fine adjacent - rather than a specific named brand asserted to be the owner's verified competitor; individual storefronts are sampled examples with provenance, never claimed rivals with measured share.

The set of per-SKU attributes observable on a public storefront without inside data - category, finish claim, materials claim, listed price, size range, positioning copy, review count - which is the only evidence base for the competitor map; anything not on the page (real cost, real margin, real units) stays [UNKNOWN].

Price brackets (e.g. mass/costume, mid fashion, premium demi-fine, fine) built from observed LISTED prices across the sample, with the listed-vs-realized-price gap (discounts, promos, bundles) flagged so the ladder is read as positioning, not as measured transaction prices.

Mapping storefront finish wording onto US FTC Jewelry Guides 16 CFR Part 23 definitions - gold-plated, gold-filled, vermeil (>=10k gold, >=2.5um, over sterling silver), rhodium (a hard bright-white platinum-group metal), sterling (92.5% Ag) - so competitor claims are comparable and vague or non-compliant claims are flagged [UNKNOWN]-quality rather than trusted as specs.

A two-axis map (typically price tier x finish/style) placing sampled competitor SKUs to reveal crowding and gaps; a gap is a whitespace HYPOTHESIS ([ESTIMATE]) to be confirmed by demand signals, never an asserted opening, because an empty cell can mean either an unmet need or an absent demand.

The [FACT-method] tests separating durable demand (persistent seasonally-adjusted baseline, breadth across cohorts and platforms, replenishment/classic nature - studs, hoops, huggies, tennis) from fad (a sharp single-platform novelty spike with a short half-life and no cross-signal confirmation), used to avoid launching into a peaking trend.

Locating a trend on the diffusion curve (emerging / growth / peak / decline) from the shape and breadth of its signals, so entry is timed: entering at emerging/growth captures durable upside while entering late at peak is the classic fad trap that leaves dead inventory.

The rule that a category or trend is treated as actionable only when >=2-3 INDEPENDENT signal families agree (e.g. search + marketplace + retail newness), so a single amplified social spike cannot by itself drive a launch decision; disagreement downgrades confidence rather than being averaged into a false middle.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for jewel_market_trend_and_competitor_mapping work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix what this trend/competitor map is FOR and the honesty boundary it works inside. It serves one decision: which fashion/costume-jewelry CATEGORIES and PRICE TIERS the owner should prioritize for a six-SKU launch, given a website already running. It is not a market-size report and produces no invented numbers: no market size, no unit-sales count, no solid-vs-plated share, no demographic rate, no price stated as measured, and no single brand asserted to be the owner's verified competitor. Every output is a ranked priority or a positioning map carrying a [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] tag. This frame binds every downstream node: a signal or competitor observation that cannot be tied to this launch-prioritization decision, or that would require fabricating a number, is out of scope.

included: the launch-prioritization decision the map serves
the no-invented-numbers and no-verified-brand honesty boundary
the tag discipline binding every output

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the launch scope or the honesty boundary changes

pros.claim: Pinning the decision the map serves keeps every signal and competitor observation load-bearing instead of decorative market trivia
pros.example: a viral novelty motif with no path to the six-SKU launch is dropped rather than reported as a finding

cons.claim: A tight decision frame can prune a genuinely useful adjacent signal that only pays off later
cons.example: an early weak signal about a new finish trend may be filtered as off-decision before it matures

failure_modes: drifting into a market-size report and inventing a headline number to fill it
naming a specific storefront as 'the competitor' with implied measured share
acceptance_tests: the launch-prioritization decision, the no-invented-numbers boundary, the no-verified-brand rule, and the tag discipline are all stated as binding on downstream nodes
revisit_triggers: the owner narrows or changes the launch scope (e.g. one category only)
kb1/kb2 hand a firmer category or buyer definition that reframes the decision
a new honesty constraint is added to the brief

nodes.definition: Enumerate the families of PUBLIC trend signal available to read US fashion-jewelry demand and fix their shared nature: (1) search-query volume (Google Trends / autocomplete / keyword tools) = demand-intent signal; (2) social-platform engagement (IG/TikTok hashtag counts, sound/audio adoption, view/like/save ratios) = attention/momentum signal; (3) marketplace signals (Amazon/Etsy best-seller rank, review velocity, 'frequently returned' flags) = ordinal sales-proxy signal; (4) retail assortment newness (new-arrival cadence, restock, sell-out badges on public storefronts) = supply-side revealed-preference signal; (5) editorial/trend-forecast (trade press, forecasters, runway/street reporting) = expert-narrative signal. All five are public, ordinal/relative, and lagged proxies for demand intent - none is a measured count of units sold. This taxonomy is the shared reference every downstream signal node and the lag/bias ledger draw on.

included: the five public signal families and their type
their shared ordinal/relative/lagged nature
the reference set the ledger tabulates
excluded: each family's detailed read method (the per-signal nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a signal family is added, removed, or re-exposed by a platform

pros.claim: A fixed signal taxonomy lets every downstream read name its source family and prevents mixing an attention signal with a sales-proxy signal
pros.example: a TikTok view spike is filed as attention/momentum, not misread as a sales figure

cons.claim: Five families is a simplification; a real signal (e.g. resale-market listings) can straddle two families
cons.example: Etsy sits between marketplace sales-proxy and social/handmade discovery, blurring the family line

failure_modes: treating any single family as 'the' demand truth
reading a cardinal magnitude out of an ordinal or attention signal
acceptance_tests: the five public signal families are enumerated with their signal type and the shared ordinal/relative/lagged caveat
revisit_triggers: a new public signal source becomes available or a platform closes its data
a platform changes how a metric is exposed (e.g. hides like counts)
the owner adds a channel that introduces a new signal family

nodes.definition: Read search-query volume (Google Trends relative index, keyword-tool volumes, autocomplete) as a demand-INTENT signal and correct for its known distortions [METHOD]. Discipline: Google Trends is a RELATIVE, sampled index (0-100 within a chosen window/geo), not an absolute count, so two queries must be compared inside one query, and index values are not unit sales; keyword-tool 'volume' is a modelled monthly estimate, not a truth. Corrections: set geo=US and a rolling window to expose seasonality (jewelry spikes at Dec/Valentine's/Mother's Day/wedding season); separate branded from generic queries; watch for the intent-to-purchase lag (search leads a first purchase but the lag varies by consideration length). Use it to rank RELATIVE demand and detect rising vs declining slope, never to state how many people buy. Tag reads [ESTIMATE] with the window and geo recorded.

included: Google Trends relative-index and keyword-volume read method
seasonality/geo/branded-vs-generic corrections
search-leads-purchase intent lag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a search-volume slope, seasonal peak, or platform index basis changes

pros.claim: Search intent is one of the earliest and least algorithmically-gamed demand signals, good for slope and relative ranking
pros.example: a steady multi-year rising slope for 'gold hoop earrings' reads as durable intent, not a spike

cons.claim: The index is relative and sampled, so it cannot size a market and small-volume niche queries are noisy
cons.example: a thin query like a specific novelty motif returns jagged, unreliable index values

failure_modes: reading the 0-100 index as an absolute count of buyers
ignoring seasonality and mistaking a December spike for durable growth
acceptance_tests: search volume is stated as a relative/sampled index compared within one query, with geo/window set, seasonality and branded-vs-generic separation, and the intent-to-purchase lag noted, and reads tagged [ESTIMATE]
revisit_triggers: a new seasonal peak or an anomalous query spike appears
the search platform changes its sampling or index basis
a branded query surge suggests a competitor campaign rather than category demand

nodes.definition: Read IG/TikTok signals (hashtag view/post counts, audio/sound adoption, engagement-rate and save ratios, creator posting cadence) as an ATTENTION/MOMENTUM signal, with heavy bias correction [METHOD]. Biases: engagement is ALGORITHMICALLY amplified (the platform pushes what already performs, exaggerating winners); content is creator- and sponsorship-CONTAMINATED (paid placements masquerade as organic demand); the audience is platform-skewed (TikTok skews younger, which matches the owner's ~18-25 target but is not the whole US market); and virality has a SHORT HALF-LIFE that overstates durable demand. Method: prefer SAVE/'add-to-favorites' and repeat-creation over raw views (saves signal purchase intent better than views); track a hashtag's slope and breadth of distinct creators, not a single viral post; discount obviously sponsored waves. Output is a momentum/attention rank, explicitly the family most prone to fad inflation, tagged [ESTIMATE] with the fad-risk flag.

included: hashtag/sound/engagement read as momentum
algorithmic-amplification, sponsorship, platform-skew and short-half-life biases
save-over-view and breadth-of-creators method

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a social trend spikes, collapses, or an algorithm/sponsorship pattern changes

pros.claim: Social is the earliest momentum signal and directly reads the owner's ~18-25 target audience's attention
pros.example: a sound adopted by hundreds of distinct creators around a category flags real emerging attention, not one viral fluke

cons.claim: It is the most fad-inflated and most manipulable family, easily mistaking amplified virality for durable demand
cons.example: a sponsored-seeded hashtag can look like organic demand and evaporate in weeks

failure_modes: reading a single viral post as category-wide durable demand
counting sponsored/seeded engagement as organic buyer intent
acceptance_tests: social engagement is read as a momentum signal with algorithmic-amplification, sponsorship, platform-skew and short-half-life biases corrected via save-over-view and breadth-of-creators, tagged [ESTIMATE] with a fad-risk flag
revisit_triggers: a hashtag or sound spikes or collapses
a platform changes its algorithm or hides engagement metrics
a sponsored campaign is detected inflating a signal

nodes.definition: Use public marketplace signals (Amazon Best Sellers Rank, Etsy 'bestseller'/'popular now' badges, review counts and review VELOCITY, star distribution, 'X sold recently' where shown) as an ORDINAL sales-proxy [METHOD]. Discipline: best-seller rank is ORDINAL (rank 1 outsells rank 2, by an unknown amount) and category-relative; it is never a unit count. Review velocity (reviews accrued per unit time) is a lagged, heavily UNDER-COUNTED proxy - only a small, self-selected fraction of buyers review, so review count is a floor on sales, not sales; the review-to-purchase ratio is itself [UNKNOWN] and varies by platform and category. Method: rank candidate categories by relative BSR and by review-velocity slope; read star distribution and 'frequently returned' flags as a quality/fit-risk signal that feeds the sizing/returns concern; treat every figure as ordinal/relative. Never multiply reviews by a made-up ratio to state units sold - that is a fabrication this node forbids.

included: best-seller rank as ordinal
review velocity as a lagged under-counted sales proxy
star/return flags as a quality-risk signal
excluded: converting reviews to a unit count (forbidden fabrication)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a marketplace rank/review-velocity or its data exposure changes

pros.claim: Marketplace rank/review velocity is the closest public proxy to actual transactions and is harder to fake than social views
pros.example: a steadily rising review velocity on a stud style across many sellers corroborates durable demand

cons.claim: It is ordinal and under-counted, so it cannot size demand and self-selected reviewers bias the picture
cons.example: a low-review new listing may still sell well, and a review-gamed listing may overstate demand

failure_modes: treating best-seller rank as a cardinal unit count
multiplying review counts by an invented review-to-sales ratio to fabricate units
acceptance_tests: best-seller rank is stated as ordinal, review velocity as a lagged under-counted proxy with an [UNKNOWN] review-to-purchase ratio, and the no-fabricated-unit-count rule is enforced
revisit_triggers: a category's best-seller rank or review velocity shifts materially
a platform changes how rank or 'sold' data is exposed
review-gaming or fake-review patterns are detected

nodes.definition: Read retail assortment NEWNESS as a supply-side revealed-preference signal [METHOD]: the cadence of new arrivals, the breadth of a category on public storefronts, restock frequency, and sell-out / 'back-in-stock' badges reveal what merchants - who have private sales data - are betting on. Discipline: this is a LAGGING signal (it reflects last season's buy-plan decided months earlier) and carries SURVIVORSHIP bias (you see what stayed on the shelf, not what failed and was pulled); a 'sold out' badge can be a merchandising tactic, not genuine scarcity. Method: track how many storefronts newly carry a category and the direction of assortment share over time; a category widening across many independent retailers is durable corroboration, while one retailer's push is weak. Output is a revealed-preference rank, explicitly lagging, tagged [ESTIMATE]; it never yields a sales number.

included: new-arrival cadence, assortment breadth, restock and sell-out badges
the lagging and survivorship-biased nature
assortment-widening across retailers as durable corroboration

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an assortment-share or restock pattern across retailers changes

pros.claim: Merchant assortment reflects parties who DO have sales data, making it a strong revealed-preference corroborator
pros.example: the same category appearing new across many independent storefronts is hard-to-fake corroboration of durable demand

cons.claim: It lags by the buy-plan cycle and is survivorship-biased, so it confirms rather than leads and can miss the newest emerging trend
cons.example: a fast emerging trend may not yet appear in assortments planned six months ago

failure_modes: reading a lagging assortment signal as a leading one and entering a trend already at peak
trusting a single retailer's push or a merchandised 'sold out' badge as genuine demand
acceptance_tests: assortment newness is read as a lagging, survivorship-biased revealed-preference signal, with cross-retailer widening as durable corroboration, tagged [ESTIMATE] and yielding no sales number
revisit_triggers: a category's assortment share widens or narrows across retailers
a wave of new arrivals or sell-outs appears in the sampled storefronts
a retailer's buy-plan cycle refreshes

nodes.definition: Compose the cross-cutting ledger that makes every signal's timing and distortion explicit so signals are interpreted, not naively averaged [FACT-method]. For each family it records: LEAD/LAG vs purchase (social leads earliest but noisiest; search leads with an intent lag; marketplace review-velocity roughly coincident-to-lagging; retail assortment lags by the buy-plan cycle; editorial varies) and its DOMINANT BIAS (social = algorithmic amplification + sponsorship; search = relative/sampled + seasonality; marketplace = ordinal + self-selected under-counted reviews; retail = survivorship + merchandising; editorial = narrative/aspirational). The operating rule: when signals disagree, the disagreement is diagnostic (e.g. social hot but search flat and marketplace cold => likely fad), and the analyst reads the pattern rather than collapsing to a single averaged score. This ledger is the interpretive spine feeding durable-vs-fad, triangulation and the honesty ledger.

included: per-family lead/lag vs purchase
per-family dominant bias
the disagreement-is-diagnostic operating rule
excluded: the durable-vs-fad discriminators built on it (DURABLE_VS_FAD_DISCRIMINATORS)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a signal family's lead/lag or bias behaviour changes

pros.claim: An explicit lag/bias ledger turns four noisy signals into an interpretable pattern and prevents naive averaging that hides fad risk
pros.example: social-hot but search-flat and marketplace-cold is read as a fad pattern instead of a middling average score

cons.claim: The lead/lag magnitudes are themselves estimates, so the ledger encodes judgement not measured lags
cons.example: the exact search-to-purchase lag for a consideration purchase is category-dependent and [ESTIMATE]

failure_modes: averaging disagreeing signals into a false-confident middle score
using a lagging signal as if it led and entering a trend late
acceptance_tests: the ledger states each family's lead/lag vs purchase and its dominant bias, plus the disagreement-is-diagnostic rule, and is consumed by durable-vs-fad and triangulation
revisit_triggers: a signal family's timing or bias behaviour changes (platform/algorithm shift)
an observed lead/lag is refuted by later purchase data
a new signal family is added to the taxonomy

nodes.definition: Define the competitor set HONESTLY as public storefront CATEGORIES, never as a specific brand asserted to be the owner's verified rival [METHOD-honesty]. The frame partitions the landscape into archetypes the owner competes against: (a) DTC plated-fashion brands (Shopify-style, curated collections, mid price); (b) marketplace sellers (Amazon/Etsy, broad, price-led); (c) fast-fashion accessory (mass, very low price, thin finish); (d) demi-fine / vermeil-adjacent (higher price, FTC-grade finish claims). Any individual storefront named is an EXEMPLAR of an archetype with recorded provenance and date, not a claim of measured competitive share or that it is 'the' competitor. This satisfies the owner's 'what brands do they buy' question by mapping the TYPES of players and how to observe them, while refusing to fabricate a verified brand-share ranking. It scopes who the sampling method will pull and which price tiers the map will span.

included: the four competitor archetypes/categories
individual storefronts as dated exemplars not verified rivals
the honest answer to 'what brands' as types-not-claims

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a competitor archetype emerges or the target tier changes

pros.claim: Framing competitors as archetypes answers the owner's brand question without fabricating a verified share ranking
pros.example: mapping DTC vs marketplace vs fast-fashion vs demi-fine tells the owner where they fit without claiming brand X is the rival

cons.claim: Archetypes lose brand-level specificity the owner may want, and archetype boundaries blur
cons.example: a DTC brand that also sells on Amazon straddles two archetypes

failure_modes: naming a specific brand as 'the owner's competitor' with implied measured share
presenting exemplars as an exhaustive verified competitor census
acceptance_tests: the competitor set is defined as public storefront archetypes with any named storefront treated as a dated exemplar, and the no-verified-brand-share rule is stated
revisit_triggers: a new competitor archetype emerges (e.g. resale/vintage platforms)
the owner narrows the target tier, changing which archetypes matter
an archetype boundary shifts (channel convergence)

nodes.definition: Give the [METHOD] to build a competitor sample from public storefronts and record its provenance and bias. Discovery paths: category search (generic queries surfacing DTC + marketplace), marketplace category browse (best-seller and new-arrival pages), social discovery (shoppable posts, creator tags), and public ad libraries (Meta Ad Library / TikTok Creative Center) to catch who is actively acquiring. For each captured storefront/SKU record source path, URL, and capture DATE (storefronts change). Sampling bias must be flagged: search/ad-library discovery over-represents heavily-marketed players and under-represents small organic sellers, so the sample is a CONVENIENCE sample, not a representative census - it supports a landscape MAP and relative tiering, not a market-share estimate. Target enough breadth per archetype and price tier that the positioning map is not driven by one or two storefronts.

included: the four discovery paths incl. ad libraries
provenance capture (source/URL/date)
convenience-sample bias flag and breadth target
excluded: which attributes to record per SKU (PUBLIC_ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the sample composition, a storefront, or a discovery path changes

pros.claim: Provenance-stamped, multi-path sampling makes the competitor map auditable and its bias explicit rather than cherry-picked
pros.example: recording capture date and source path lets a later reviewer re-pull and see what changed

cons.claim: Public discovery is a convenience sample skewed to marketed players, so it cannot support a share estimate and undercounts small sellers
cons.example: an ad-library-led sample over-weights brands currently running paid campaigns

failure_modes: treating a convenience sample as a representative census and inferring market share
sampling too few storefronts so one or two dominate the map
acceptance_tests: the discovery paths, per-SKU provenance (source/URL/date), the convenience-sample bias flag, and the per-archetype breadth target are all stated
revisit_triggers: storefronts in the sample change or go offline
a new discovery path or ad library becomes available
the map is found to hinge on too few storefronts

nodes.definition: Fix the schema of PUBLICLY OBSERVABLE attributes to record per competitor SKU - the only evidence base for the map [METHOD]. Fields: category (stud/hoop/drop; chain/pendant; ring; bracelet; anklet), finish claim (verbatim copy, e.g. '18k gold plated', 'vermeil', 'rhodium-plated silver', 'tarnish-free'), materials/base claim, listed price, any promo/'compare-at' price shown, size/length range offered, positioning copy/style language, review count and star rating, and shipping/return terms if shown. The hard boundary: only what is on the public page is recorded; real production cost, real margin, real units sold, and true finish quality are NOT observable and stay [UNKNOWN] - they are never inferred as if measured. Finish claims are captured VERBATIM here for normalization downstream, not trusted as verified specs. This schema standardizes the sample so price-tiering and positioning are comparable across storefronts.

included: the observable per-SKU fields incl. verbatim finish claim and listed/promo price
the [UNKNOWN] boundary for cost/margin/units/true quality
verbatim capture for downstream normalization

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an observable attribute becomes available or unobservable

pros.claim: A fixed observable schema keeps the map strictly evidence-based and marks the [UNKNOWN] boundary so nothing off-page is fabricated
pros.example: recording listed price but leaving margin blank stops a made-up competitor-cost claim

cons.claim: Observable attributes miss what most matters commercially (real cost, real sales), so the map describes positioning not performance
cons.example: two SKUs at the same listed price may have wildly different real margins the schema cannot see

failure_modes: inferring real cost/margin/units from observable attributes as if measured
trusting verbatim finish copy as a verified quality spec at capture time
acceptance_tests: the observable per-SKU fields are enumerated, finish claims captured verbatim, and cost/margin/units/true-quality marked [UNKNOWN] and never inferred as measured

nodes.definition: Build a price-tier ladder from the sample's LISTED prices [METHOD]. Cluster observed listed prices per category into brackets - illustratively mass/costume (low), mid fashion, premium demi-fine/vermeil, and fine-adjacent - with bracket cut points set from the observed distribution (natural gaps / quantiles), not from invented thresholds, and always per-category (a stud ladder differs from a statement-necklace ladder). Critical caveat: LISTED price is not REALIZED price - discounts, 'compare-at' anchoring, promo cadence, bundles and returns move realized price, and the listed-vs-realized gap is [UNKNOWN] per storefront; the ladder therefore describes POSITIONING, not measured transaction prices. This directly serves the owner's 'what's the price' question by mapping the public price STRUCTURE and where the owner's fashion/costume tier sits, without asserting any price as a measured sale. Output feeds the positioning map's price axis.

included: per-category listed-price brackets from the observed distribution
the listed-vs-realized price gap flagged [UNKNOWN]
ladder as positioning not transaction prices
excluded: placing SKUs on the two-axis map (POSITIONING_MAP)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the listed-price distribution or discount pattern shifts

pros.claim: A data-driven per-category ladder answers 'what's the price' as a public structure without fabricating a realized transaction price
pros.example: showing four listed-price bands for hoops locates the owner's target band against the field

cons.claim: Listed prices overstate what buyers actually pay in a discount-heavy category, so the ladder can misplace tiers
cons.example: a brand permanently '40% off' lists high but realizes mid, distorting its apparent tier

failure_modes: quoting a listed price as a measured realized/transaction price
using invented round-number thresholds instead of the observed distribution
acceptance_tests: per-category price brackets are built from the observed listed-price distribution, the listed-vs-realized gap is flagged [UNKNOWN], and the ladder is stated as positioning not measured transaction prices
revisit_triggers: a wave of discounting shifts listed vs realized prices
the sample expands and the bracket cut points move
a new price tier appears in the field

nodes.definition: Normalize captured finish claims against the US FTC Jewelry Guides 16 CFR Part 23 so competitor claims are comparable and puffery is flagged [FACT-16 CFR 23]. Reference definitions: gold-plated = a layer of gold (>=10k) mechanically/electrolytically bonded, no minimum thickness for 'plated' alone; gold-filled = a thick mechanically bonded gold layer >=1/20 by weight; vermeil = >=10k gold, >=2.5 micrometers thick, over STERLING silver; rhodium = a platinum-group white metal (hard, bright, tarnish-resistant) commonly plated over sterling silver or white gold; sterling = 92.5% Ag. Method: map each verbatim claim to the nearest FTC term, mark whether the claim MEETS the definition or is vague/aspirational ('tarnish-free', '18k gold' on obviously plated goods, unqualified 'gold'), and flag non-compliant or unverifiable claims as [UNKNOWN]-quality rather than trusting the copy. This makes the finish axis of the map honest and connects competitor claims to the owner's real materials story (S2). It classifies claims; it does not assay the actual metal.

included: the FTC 16 CFR 23 finish definitions as [FACT]
mapping verbatim claims to FTC terms and flagging non-compliant/vague ones
finish comparability for the map
excluded: the owner's own finish engineering (S2 materials)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the FTC guides or the field's finish-claim patterns change

pros.claim: Anchoring finish claims to 16 CFR 23 makes competitor quality claims comparable and exposes puffery instead of trusting marketing copy
pros.example: a 'vermeil' claim can be checked against the >=10k / >=2.5um / over-sterling test and flagged if unqualified

cons.claim: Public copy cannot be assayed, so normalization classifies the CLAIM, not the true metal, leaving real quality [UNKNOWN]
cons.example: a compliant-sounding 'vermeil' label may still be over-stated and cannot be verified from the page

failure_modes: treating a marketing finish claim as a verified metallurgical spec
misapplying an FTC term (e.g. conflating gold-filled with gold-plated)
acceptance_tests: captured finish claims are mapped to the FTC 16 CFR 23 definitions (gold-plated / gold-filled / vermeil >=10k >=2.5um over sterling / rhodium / sterling 92.5%), with non-compliant or vague claims flagged [UNKNOWN]-quality
revisit_triggers: the FTC updates the Jewelry Guides

nodes.definition: Assemble the competitor positioning MAP from the normalized attributes [METHOD]. Place sampled SKUs/storefronts on two axes - typically price tier (from PRICE_TIER_LADDER) against finish/quality claim (from FINISH_CLAIM_NORMALIZATION), with style family (minimalist / statement / trend-motif) as an optional third cut. The output is a MAP that shows where the field clusters and where the owner's fashion/costume tier sits relative to it - not a ranked league table of who is 'best'. Density (how many SKUs occupy each cell) and archetype colouring make crowding visible. Every point carries its provenance and its [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tags (position is from listed price and claimed finish, both caveated). This is the synthesized competitive-landscape artifact the owner asked for ('what brands, what shapes, what price' as a structure), and it is the substrate the whitespace read operates on.

included: the price x finish (optional x style) two/three-axis map
cell density and archetype colouring for crowding
map-not-league-table framing with tags

nodes.definition: Read the positioning map for crowding and whitespace as HYPOTHESES, not asserted openings [METHOD/ESTIMATE]. Identify cells that are dense (crowded, price-competitive, hard to enter) and cells that are sparse in the owner's fashion/costume tier. The disciplined caveat: an empty cell is AMBIGUOUS - it can mean an unmet need (real whitespace) OR an absent/served-elsewhere demand (a dead zone no one profitably occupies). Therefore every gap is a whitespace HYPOTHESIS that must be confirmed by DEMAND signals (search/marketplace/retail) before it is treated as an opportunity; a gap with no supporting demand signal is a trap, not an opening. Output is a short list of candidate whitespace cells, each tagged [ESTIMATE] with the demand-confirmation status still pending, feeding the durability score and, ultimately, the assortment decision.

included: crowded vs sparse cell reading
the empty-cell ambiguity (unmet need vs dead zone)
gap-as-hypothesis-pending-demand-confirmation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the map or a gap's demand-confirmation status changes

pros.claim: Treating whitespace as a hypothesis to be demand-confirmed prevents the classic 'empty cell = opportunity' error
pros.example: a sparse ultra-premium costume cell is flagged pending demand rather than declared an opening

cons.claim: Ambiguity means whitespace reads are low-confidence until triangulated, so they cannot drive a decision alone
cons.example: a genuine emerging gap and a dead zone look identical on the map before demand confirmation

failure_modes: declaring an empty map cell an opportunity without demand confirmation
ignoring that a crowded cell can still be enter-able with a differentiated finish/price
acceptance_tests: crowded and sparse cells are identified, the empty-cell ambiguity is stated, and each gap is output as an [ESTIMATE] whitespace hypothesis pending demand confirmation
revisit_triggers: the positioning map changes
a demand signal confirms or refutes a candidate gap
a competitor enters a previously sparse cell

nodes.definition: State the discriminators that separate DURABLE demand from FAD [FACT-method], the core of not launching into a peaking trend. Durable demand shows: a PERSISTENT seasonally-adjusted baseline over multiple years (not a single spike); BREADTH across cohorts, platforms and signal families; a REPLENISHMENT/classic nature (staples repurchased and gifted - studs, small hoops, huggies, tennis chains, thin bands); and low novelty-dependence. Fad shows: a sharp SINGLE-PLATFORM spike with a short half-life; a specific NOVELTY MOTIF tied to one moment/creator; steep decline after peak; and no cross-signal confirmation (social-only). The method scores each candidate category on duration, baseline persistence, breadth, and replenishment vs novelty, using the lag/bias ledger to weight signals. This is the honest answer to 'which types sell durably' - it flags fad risk rather than chasing virality - and it feeds lifecycle staging and the durability score. Tag category calls [ESTIMATE] with the discriminators cited.

included: durable-demand discriminators (persistence, breadth, replenishment)
fad discriminators (single-platform spike, novelty motif, short half-life)
scoring candidates on the discriminators
excluded: placing a trend on the diffusion curve (TREND_LIFECYCLE_STAGING)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a category's durability/fad signal pattern changes

pros.claim: Explicit durable-vs-fad tests protect a small six-SKU launch from committing inventory to a peaking novelty
pros.example: a classic small-hoop staple scores durable while a single-season charm motif scores fad and is deprioritized

cons.claim: Some fads convert to durable (yesterday's fad becomes a staple), so the binary can misclassify an emerging durable trend early
cons.example: a motif that looks faddish early may broaden into a lasting category, risking a false-fad rejection

failure_modes: chasing a social-only viral spike as if it were durable demand
rejecting an emerging durable trend as a fad because it is early and narrow
acceptance_tests: the durable discriminators (persistence, breadth, replenishment) and fad discriminators (single-platform spike, novelty motif, short half-life) are stated and applied to score candidate categories [ESTIMATE]
revisit_triggers: a category's signal breadth or baseline persistence shifts
a prior fad broadens into durable demand or vice versa
the lag/bias ledger weighting changes

nodes.definition: Place a trend on the diffusion/lifecycle curve - emerging, growth, peak, decline - to time entry [METHOD]. Read the shape and breadth of a trend's signals: emerging = narrow early social/search rise, low assortment presence; growth = accelerating across multiple signal families and widening assortment; peak = broad saturation, ubiquitous assortment, flattening search, heavy discounting starting; decline = falling search/engagement and clearance. The decision consequence: entering at emerging/growth captures durable upside and margin, while entering LATE at peak - when assortment is saturated and discounting has begun - is the classic fad trap that leaves a small launch holding dead, marked-down inventory. Because retail assortment LAGS, a category that is only now saturating shelves may already be peaking. Output is a stage label per candidate with an entry-timing recommendation, tagged [ESTIMATE]; it consumes the durable-vs-fad read and feeds the durability score.

included: the four lifecycle stages and their signal signatures
entry-timing consequence (early upside vs late-peak trap)
the assortment-lag caution on reading saturation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a trend's lifecycle stage or discounting onset changes

pros.claim: Staging times entry so the launch rides growth rather than buying into a peak
pros.example: a category still in growth across search+marketplace is a better six-SKU bet than one already saturating shelves

cons.claim: Stage boundaries are fuzzy and lagging signals can make a peaking trend look like it is still growing
cons.example: assortment only now widening can mask that search already peaked months ago

failure_modes: entering late at peak when discounting has already started
mistaking a lagging assortment rise for early growth
acceptance_tests: each candidate gets a lifecycle stage from its signal signature with an entry-timing recommendation, and the late-at-peak fad trap and assortment-lag caution are stated, tagged [ESTIMATE]
revisit_triggers: a trend's signal shape shifts stage (growth to peak)
discounting or clearance begins in a category
search flattens while assortment still widens

nodes.definition: Impose the triangulation gate: a category or trend is treated as ACTIONABLE only when >=2-3 INDEPENDENT signal families agree in direction [METHOD]. Independence matters - search + marketplace + retail-newness are more independent than three social metrics, which share the same amplification. The gate uses the lag/bias ledger: agreement across families that lead and lag differently is stronger than agreement within one family. It converts the whitespace hypotheses into confirmed or rejected openings (a sparse cell WITH converging demand signals is a real opportunity; a sparse cell with none is a dead zone). Single-signal traps it prevents: a viral TikTok spike with flat search and cold marketplace (fad), or a crowded assortment with no consumer-side demand (over-supplied). When signals DISagree, confidence is downgraded and the item is held for more evidence rather than averaged into a false middle. Output: an actionability flag per candidate with the confirming signals named, tagged [ESTIMATE].

included: the >=2-3 independent-family agreement rule
converting whitespace hypotheses to confirmed/rejected
downgrade-on-disagreement instead of averaging

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a candidate's cross-signal agreement status changes

pros.claim: Requiring independent-family agreement blocks single-signal fad and over-supply traps before capital is committed
pros.example: a gap confirmed by rising search AND marketplace velocity AND assortment widening is a real opening, not a guess

cons.claim: Demanding multi-signal agreement can reject a genuine early trend that only one leading signal has caught yet
cons.example: a real emerging category may show only in early social before search or marketplace catch up, and be held back

failure_modes: acting on a single amplified signal without independent confirmation
averaging disagreeing signals into a false-confident middle instead of downgrading
acceptance_tests: actionability requires >=2-3 independent signal families to agree, whitespace hypotheses are confirmed or rejected accordingly, and disagreement downgrades rather than averages, with confirming signals named [ESTIMATE]
revisit_triggers: a previously single-signal item gains or loses independent confirmation

a new independent signal family becomes available

nodes.definition: Compose the honest, caveated ranking that the assortment decision consumes [ESTIMATE]. For each candidate category/tier, combine: durable-demand strength (from DURABLE_VS_FAD_DISCRIMINATORS + lifecycle stage), competitive whitespace/enter-ability (from WHITESPACE_DETECTION), and triangulation confidence (from SIGNAL_TRIANGULATION). The composite is explicitly an ORDINAL RANKING of candidates, not a cardinal forecast of sales or share - it says 'prioritize A over B for the launch', never 'A will sell N units'. Weights are transparent and adjustable; confidence per candidate reflects how many independent signals confirmed it. Low-triangulation or fad-flagged candidates are ranked down or held regardless of a hot single signal. The score is tagged [ESTIMATE] with its inputs and confidence, and every candidate that relies on an unconfirmed whitespace or a lagging signal carries that caveat. This is the load-bearing synthesis feeding S5 assortment.

transparent adjustable weights and per-candidate confidence
ranking-not-forecast framing
excluded: the final SKU pick and production constraints (S5 assortment)

pros.example: durable + whitespace-confirmed + triangulated categories rank above a hot but fad-flagged single-signal one

cons.claim: Any composite hides tradeoffs in its weights and can look more precise than its [ESTIMATE] inputs justify
cons.example: a small weight change can reorder mid-pack candidates, so the ranking is directional not exact

failure_modes: reading the ordinal ranking as a cardinal sales/share forecast
letting an opaque weight bury a fad-flagged candidate's risk
acceptance_tests: candidates are ranked ordinally by combining durability, whitespace and triangulation with transparent weights and per-candidate confidence, framed as a priority ranking not a sales forecast, tagged [ESTIMATE]
revisit_triggers: an input (durability, whitespace, lifecycle, triangulation) updates for any candidate
the weights are re-tuned
S5 requests a re-ranking under new constraints

nodes.definition: Maintain the honesty ledger that separates what is known from what is inferred from what is unknowable here, enforcing the brief's non-negotiable boundary. [FACT] anchors: the FTC 16 CFR 23 finish definitions, the ordinal/relative/lagged nature of each signal family, and the durable-vs-fad method itself. [ESTIMATE] (method+confidence): the price-tier ladder, the positioning map cell placements, whitespace hypotheses, lifecycle stages, triangulation flags, and the durability ranking. [UNKNOWN] (never fabricated): actual market size, unit-sales counts, solid-vs-plated share, any competitor's real cost/margin/units, true finish quality behind a claim, realized (vs listed) prices, and any single brand's verified competitive share. The ledger also forbids the specific fabrications: no named brand as 'the owner's verified competitor', no reviews-times-a-ratio unit count, no listed price quoted as measured. It governs how every hand-off statement is phrased so direction is trusted and level is never over-read.

included: the [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] partition of every output
the explicit list of forbidden fabrications
governing hand-off phrasing

nodes.definition: Compose the hand-off to the assortment specialist (S5) and back to kb1/kb2. Deliver: (1) the ordinal ranked category/tier priorities from DEMAND_DURABILITY_SCORE with per-candidate confidence and durable-vs-fad flags; (2) the competitor positioning map with its price ladder and normalized finish axis; (3) the confirmed vs rejected whitespace cells; each carrying its [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tag from the honesty ledger. It states the binding conditions the assortment decision must respect: re-triangulate before committing a fad-flagged candidate, treat every price as positioning not realized, and treat the competitor set as archetypes not verified rivals. It STOPS before the six-SKU pick, the production/MOQ constraints, and the poll instrument - those belong to S5 and S4. This is the load-bearing output of the KB: a decision-ready but honestly-bounded demand-and-competitor read.

conflict_axes.name: social_momentum_vs_marketplace_evidence
conflict_axes.description: Social engagement is the earliest signal but the most fad-inflated, while marketplace rank/review-velocity is closer to transactions but lagging; they often disagree on the same category.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: log both in the lag/bias ledger and require triangulation; read social-hot-but-marketplace-cold as a fad pattern, not an average

conflict_axes.name: empty_cell_opportunity_vs_dead_zone
conflict_axes.description: A sparse positioning-map cell can be genuine unmet-demand whitespace or a dead zone no one profitably occupies; the map alone cannot tell them apart.
poles: treat the gap as an opportunity
treat the gap as a dead zone
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold every gap as a hypothesis until >=2-3 independent demand signals confirm it; unconfirmed gaps are dead zones

conflict_axes.name: leading_noisy_vs_lagging_reliable_signals
conflict_axes.description: Leading signals (social, search) catch trends early but are noisy; lagging signals (marketplace, retail assortment) are more reliable but confirm late, so timing and reliability trade off.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the lag/bias ledger to weight by independence and stage on the diffusion curve; enter in growth, not at lagging-confirmed peak

conflict_axes.name: durable_staple_vs_trend_novelty
conflict_axes.description: Durable staples (studs, hoops, huggies) offer safe replenishment demand but thin differentiation, while trend novelty offers attention and margin but short half-life and fad risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight the six-SKU launch toward durable-confirmed categories and admit at most a bounded, triangulated novelty bet

conflict_axes.name: listed_price_vs_realized_price
conflict_axes.description: Listed storefront prices are observable but discount/promo cadence makes realized price [UNKNOWN], so a price ladder built on listings can misplace a discounter's true tier.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: build the ladder from listed prices but label it positioning-only and flag heavy-discounter distortion; never quote listed as realized

conflict_axes.name: verified_brand_naming_vs_archetype_honesty
conflict_axes.description: The owner wants to know 'what brands' but naming a specific storefront as a verified competitor with implied share is a fabrication; archetypes answer honestly but lose brand specificity.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: map archetypes and cite individual storefronts only as dated exemplars, never as verified rivals with measured share

conflict_axes.name: ordinal_signal_vs_cardinal_number_demand
conflict_axes.description: Stakeholders want cardinal numbers (how many buy, what share) but public signals are ordinal/relative; converting them to counts fabricates precision.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: deliver ordinal rankings and relative slopes with [ESTIMATE] tags; leave true counts/shares as [UNKNOWN] to be measured by poll/public-data pulls

conflict_axes.name: convenience_sample_breadth_vs_effort
conflict_axes.description: A broader storefront sample makes the map more robust but costs effort, while a thin sample is fast but lets one or two storefronts drive the whole positioning map.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sample enough breadth per archetype and price tier that no single storefront drives a cell, and stamp provenance so it can be re-pulled

conflict_axes.name: single_hot_signal_vs_triangulated_confidence
conflict_axes.description: A single hot signal invites a fast decision, but acting before independent confirmation risks a fad or over-supply trap; triangulation is safer but slower and can reject a true early trend.
poles: act on the strongest single signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require >=2-3 independent families for an actionable call; downgrade rather than average on disagreement, and revisit held early-trend candidates as signals mature

edge_cases.description: A category is hot on TikTok with high views but shows flat search and cold marketplace review-velocity
edge_cases.trigger: a single social family spikes while independent families stay flat
edge_cases.mitigation: flag as a probable fad; withhold from the launch shortlist until >=2 independent families confirm, and log the disagreement rather than averaging

edge_cases.description: A sparse positioning-map cell is declared a whitespace opportunity with no demand signal behind it
edge_cases.trigger: an empty cell is read as an opening without triangulated demand confirmation
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the gap as a hypothesis pending demand confirmation; if no independent signal supports it, classify it a dead zone

edge_cases.description: A competitor's listed price is quoted downstream as the price buyers actually pay
edge_cases.trigger: a listed or 'compare-at' price is treated as a realized transaction price
edge_cases.mitigation: label the ladder positioning-only, flag the listed-vs-realized gap [UNKNOWN], and note heavy-discounter distortion

edge_cases.description: A specific storefront is written up as 'the owner's competitor' with an implied market share
edge_cases.trigger: an exemplar storefront is elevated to a verified rival with a fabricated share claim
edge_cases.mitigation: demote it to a dated archetype exemplar; state no verified brand-share is measurable from public data

edge_cases.description: Review counts are multiplied by an assumed review-to-sales ratio to state units sold
edge_cases.trigger: an analyst converts an ordinal/under-counted review signal into a cardinal unit count
edge_cases.mitigation: keep review velocity ordinal; leave the review-to-purchase ratio and unit count [UNKNOWN]; never fabricate units

edge_cases.description: Retail assortment is only now widening for a category whose search already peaked months ago
edge_cases.trigger: a lagging assortment signal is read as early growth
edge_cases.mitigation: discount the lagging signal against leading search; stage the trend at peak and flag late-entry inventory risk

edge_cases.description: A 'vermeil' or '18k gold' claim is trusted as a verified spec on obviously plated costume goods
edge_cases.trigger: marketing finish copy is treated as a measured metallurgical fact
edge_cases.mitigation: test the claim against 16 CFR 23 (>=10k, >=2.5um, over sterling for vermeil) and flag non-compliant or unqualified claims [UNKNOWN]-quality

edge_cases.description: The positioning map hinges on one or two storefronts because the sample was too thin
edge_cases.trigger: a cell's position is driven by a single sampled storefront
edge_cases.mitigation: expand the sample per archetype and price tier until no single storefront drives a cell; re-pull using stored provenance

edge_cases.description: A seasonal December/Valentine's search spike is read as durable year-round growth
edge_cases.trigger: an un-deseasonalized search peak is mistaken for a rising baseline
edge_cases.mitigation: use a rolling window and seasonally adjust; require multi-year baseline persistence before calling demand durable

edge_cases.description: Signals disagree and are averaged into a middling composite score that hides the conflict
edge_cases.trigger: conflicting signals are numerically averaged instead of interpreted
edge_cases.mitigation: downgrade confidence on disagreement and surface the conflict pattern; never collapse a genuine disagreement into a false middle

edge_cases.description: A sponsored/seeded hashtag wave is counted as organic consumer demand
edge_cases.trigger: paid influencer placement is mistaken for organic engagement
edge_cases.mitigation: discount obviously sponsored waves, prefer save/repeat-creation over views, and require independent-family confirmation

edge_cases.description: A candidate rejected early as a fad later broadens into durable demand and is missed
edge_cases.trigger: a false-fad rejection is never revisited as signals mature
edge_cases.mitigation: hold early-narrow candidates on a watchlist and re-triangulate as breadth grows rather than permanently discarding

workflow.action: Fix the decision frame and honesty boundary
workflow.description: State that the map serves the six-SKU category/tier prioritization and forbids invented numbers and verified-brand claims
workflow.gate: the launch-prioritization decision, the no-invented-numbers boundary and the no-verified-brand rule are stated

workflow.description: Enumerate search, social, marketplace, retail-newness and editorial families as public, ordinal, lagged
workflow.gate: the five signal families are listed with type and the ordinal/lagged caveat

workflow.action: Read each signal with its corrections
workflow.description: Apply the read method and bias corrections to search, social, marketplace and retail signals
workflow.gate: each signal is read with its relative/ordinal caveat and its dominant bias corrected, tagged [ESTIMATE]

workflow.description: Tabulate each family's lead/lag vs purchase and dominant bias with the disagreement-is-diagnostic rule
workflow.gate: per-family lead/lag and bias are tabulated and the disagreement rule is stated

workflow.action: Define the competitor frame and sample storefronts
workflow.description: Frame competitors as archetypes and build a provenance-stamped convenience sample from public discovery paths
workflow.gate: archetypes are defined, storefronts sampled with source/URL/date, and convenience-sample bias flagged

workflow.action: Record observable attributes and build the price ladder
workflow.description: Capture the observable per-SKU schema and cluster listed prices into per-category tiers
workflow.gate: observable attributes are recorded, cost/margin/units left [UNKNOWN], and per-category listed-price tiers built with the realized-price caveat

workflow.action: Normalize finish claims against FTC 16 CFR 23
workflow.description: Map verbatim finish claims to FTC definitions and flag vague/non-compliant claims
workflow.gate: finish claims are mapped to 16 CFR 23 terms with non-compliant/vague claims flagged [UNKNOWN]-quality

workflow.action: Assemble the positioning map and read whitespace
workflow.description: Place SKUs on price x finish (x style) axes and identify crowded vs sparse cells as hypotheses
workflow.gate: the map is built with density/archetype colouring and whitespace cells output as [ESTIMATE] hypotheses

workflow.action: Separate durable demand from fad and stage the lifecycle
workflow.description: Score candidates on persistence/breadth/replenishment and place each on the diffusion curve
workflow.gate: durable-vs-fad discriminators are applied and each candidate gets a lifecycle stage with entry timing

workflow.description: Confirm or reject candidates and whitespace using >=2-3 independent signal families
workflow.gate: each candidate has an actionability flag requiring independent-family agreement, with disagreements downgraded

workflow.action: Compose the durability x whitespace ranking
workflow.description: Combine durability, whitespace and triangulation into a transparent ordinal candidate ranking
workflow.gate: candidates are ranked ordinally with transparent weights and per-candidate confidence, framed as priority not forecast

workflow.action: Apply the honesty ledger and compose the hand-off
workflow.description: Tag every output [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] and hand off ranked priorities + map + whitespace verdicts with binding conditions
workflow.gate: the ranked priorities, positioning map and whitespace verdicts are handed off with tags and binding conditions, stopping before the SKU pick

priority_rationale: The decision frame and signal taxonomy come first because they scope which signals and competitors are worth reading and set the honesty boundary; the four per-signal reads and the lag/bias ledger next, because every trend judgement depends on reading each signal with its own lag and bias rather than at face value; the competitor frame, sampling, attribute schema, price ladder and finish normalization then build the observable evidence base honestly; the positioning map and whitespace read synthesize that base into a landscape; the durable-vs-fad, lifecycle and triangulation nodes separate signal from noise and time entry; and the durability score, honesty ledger and hand-off come last because they compose the ranked, tagged, decision-ready output and stop cleanly before the SKU pick.

dominance_rules.rule: Triangulated agreement dominates any single hot signal
dominance_rules.rationale: a single amplified signal (especially social) is the top source of fad and over-supply traps
dominance_rules.trigger: a decision rests on one signal family without independent confirmation
dominance_rules.action: require >=2-3 independent families to agree before treating the candidate as actionable

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty [UNKNOWN] dominates stakeholder pressure for a number
dominance_rules.rationale: market size, unit counts, solid-vs-plated share and competitor units are not measurable from public signals
dominance_rules.trigger: a request to state a cardinal market/share/units figure
dominance_rules.action: deliver a method or ordinal ranking and leave the true count [UNKNOWN] for the poll/public-data pull

dominance_rules.rationale: naming a storefront as a verified competitor with share is a fabrication the brief forbids
dominance_rules.trigger: an urge to name a specific brand as the owner's competitor
dominance_rules.action: map archetypes and cite storefronts only as dated exemplars, never as measured rivals

dominance_rules.rule: Demand confirmation dominates an empty-cell whitespace read
dominance_rules.rationale: an empty positioning-map cell is as likely a dead zone as an opportunity
dominance_rules.trigger: a sparse cell is proposed as a launch opening
dominance_rules.action: hold it as a hypothesis until independent demand signals confirm; otherwise treat it as a dead zone

dominance_rules.rule: Leading-signal staging dominates lagging assortment when they conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: retail assortment lags the buy-plan cycle and can flag a peaking trend as growing
dominance_rules.trigger: assortment widening suggests growth while leading search has flattened
dominance_rules.action: stage the trend at peak on the leading signal and flag late-entry inventory risk

dominance_rules.rule: Positioning-only pricing dominates any listed-as-realized quote
dominance_rules.rationale: discounts and promos make realized price [UNKNOWN], so listed prices describe positioning only
dominance_rules.trigger: a listed price is about to be used as a measured transaction price
dominance_rules.action: state the ladder as positioning, flag the listed-vs-realized gap, and refuse the measured-price claim

dominance_rules.rule: Durable-confirmed demand dominates novelty in the launch weighting
dominance_rules.rationale: a small six-SKU launch cannot absorb dead fad inventory
dominance_rules.trigger: a hot novelty motif competes with a durable staple for a launch slot
dominance_rules.action: weight toward durable-confirmed categories and cap novelty to a bounded, triangulated bet

dominance_rules.rationale: averaging conflicting signals hides the diagnostic pattern (e.g. social-hot/marketplace-cold = fad)
dominance_rules.trigger: conflicting signals are about to be averaged into one score
dominance_rules.action: downgrade confidence and surface the conflict pattern instead of collapsing to a false middle

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the decision frame and honesty boundary before reading any signal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: collecting market trivia and inventing numbers that must later be stripped out as off-decision or fabricated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stamp provenance (source/URL/date) on every sampled storefront at capture
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unre-pullable, un-auditable competitor map that must be rebuilt when storefronts change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture finish claims verbatim and normalize against 16 CFR 23 in the same pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an incomparable finish axis and trusted marketing puffery that must be re-audited later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the price ladder from listed prices with the realized-price caveat attached from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a listed price circulating as a measured transaction price and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tags to each output when first produced, not at the end
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an estimate hardening into an asserted fact that must be walked back downstream

anti_rework_rules.rule: Require triangulation before promoting any candidate or whitespace to actionable
anti_rework_rules.prevents: committing the launch to a single-signal fad and re-doing the shortlist after it collapses

anti_rework_rules.rule: Deseasonalize search and require multi-year persistence before calling demand durable
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a seasonal spike being mislabelled durable and driving a mistimed launch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep marketplace signals ordinal and never derive unit counts from reviews
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fabricated unit-sales figure propagating into the assortment and economics models

iteration_protocol.trigger: a signal family spikes, collapses, or a platform changes how a metric is exposed
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the affected signal and update its row in the lag/bias ledger

iteration_protocol.trigger: a candidate's cross-signal agreement changes (a single-signal item gains or loses independent confirmation)
iteration_protocol.action: re-run triangulation and re-score the affected candidates

iteration_protocol.trigger: storefronts in the sample change, go offline, or the sample proves too thin
iteration_protocol.action: re-pull using stored provenance, expand breadth, and rebuild the price ladder and positioning map

iteration_protocol.trigger: a wave of discounting shifts listed vs realized prices in the field
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the price-tier ladder and re-flag the listed-vs-realized gap

iteration_protocol.trigger: a trend crosses a lifecycle stage or discounting/clearance begins
iteration_protocol.action: re-stage the trend and re-time entry, updating the durability score

iteration_protocol.trigger: the FTC Jewelry Guides update or a new finish-claim pattern appears
iteration_protocol.action: update the finish normalization and re-flag affected competitor claims

iteration_protocol.trigger: S5 assortment requests a re-scoped or re-weighted hand-off
iteration_protocol.action: re-tune the scoring weights and recompose the hand-off under the new constraints
